name: Duty of oversight

subjectOf.text: The liability standard for breach of fiduciary duty is set so high that courts rarely find directors in violation, because only a board's sustained or systematic failure to exercise oversight can produce liability.
subjectOf.abstract: The standard for liability is so high that it is hard for courts to find directors in violation of their fiduciary duties.2 Only a board's sustained or systematic failure to exercise oversight can result in liability.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Elizabeth R. Malay, The Role of Corporate Integrity Agreements in the Expansion of Fiduciary Duties (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2317580
scope_conditions: director oversight liability under Caremark and its progeny

subjectOf.text: Although CIAs are not laws, they go beyond aspirational governance standards because they set forth concrete governance rules that more clearly define the duties to be informed, to exercise oversight, and to maintain effective reporting systems, thereby requiring a higher standard of care.
subjectOf.abstract: Although CIAs are not laws, they do go beyond aspirational governance standards. CIAs set forth concrete governance rules that expand the fiduciary duties of directors.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Elizabeth R. Malay, The Role of Corporate Integrity Agreements in the Expansion of Fiduciary Duties (2013). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2317580
scope_conditions: directors of companies operating under a CIA

subjectOf.text: The nearly insurmountable standard for liability in oversight cases in the United States undermines the signalling of the expected standard of conduct, and this could have long-term implications for American corporate law.
subjectOf.abstract: The nearly insurmountable standard for liability in oversight cases and its effect on signalling the expected standard of conduct could have long-term implications for corporate law in the United States.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, A Comparative Perspective on the Limitations of the Duty of Oversight – A Comment on Lisa Fairfax (2013)
scope_conditions: oversight or duty to monitor claims

subjectOf.text: Stable rules may not suffice to make directors' oversight role more robust, so contractual and quasi law forms of dynamic governance are a promising supplement for improving the duty of oversight.
subjectOf.abstract: After outlining why stable rules may not suffice to make directors' oversight role more robust, the author provides some initial thoughts on how contractual and quasi law forms of dynamic governance could help improve the duty of oversight.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, A Comparative Perspective on the Limitations of the Duty of Oversight – A Comment on Lisa Fairfax (2013)

subjectOf.text: Without a workable duty of oversight, corporate directors who seek to comply with the oversight duty lack meaningful guidance about the conduct expected of them.
subjectOf.abstract: Without a workable duty of oversight, corporate directors seeking to comply with the oversight duty lack meaningful guidance as to the expected conduct.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, A Comparative Perspective on the Limitations of the Duty of Oversight – A Comment on Lisa Fairfax (2013)
scope_conditions: doctrine of oversight remains immature and incoherent

subjectOf.text: Because directors serve part-time as outsiders, it is unreasonable to expect them to have the knowledge, capacity, and expertise needed to monitor effectively the business affairs of large and increasingly complex corporations.
subjectOf.abstract: that, because directors serve part-time as outsiders, it may be unreasonable to expect directors to have the knowledge, capacity, and expertise to "effectively monitor the
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, A Comparative Perspective on the Limitations of the Duty of Oversight – A Comment on Lisa Fairfax (2013)

subjectOf.text: Delaware's signalling of expected conduct is undermined when the state simultaneously imposes a near insurmountable standard for liability in cases involving breaches of the duty of oversight.
subjectOf.abstract: Most importantly, Professor Fairfax explains why, while Delaware law may signal the most appropriate standard of conduct, 15 Delaware's signaling of expected conduct is undermined if it imposes a near insurmountable standard for liability in cases involving breaches of the duty of oversight.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, A Comparative Perspective on the Limitations of the Duty of Oversight – A Comment on Lisa Fairfax (2013)

subjectOf.text: Germany has taken a much stricter approach than the United States to cases involving a breach of the duty of oversight, even though the German business judgment rule formally requires a showing of the same elements as the American one.
subjectOf.abstract: For instance, Germany has taken a much stricter approach to cases involving a breach of the duty of oversight.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, A Comparative Perspective on the Limitations of the Duty of Oversight – A Comment on Lisa Fairfax (2013)
scope_conditions: comparison of German and Delaware corporate law

subjectOf.text: The German ARAG/Garmenbeck holding is diametrically opposed to In re Citigroup, where the Delaware Chancery Court declared that directors' incorrect evaluation of business risk did not violate the duty of oversight.
subjectOf.abstract: This holding is diametrically opposed to the holding in In re Citigroup where the Delaware Chancery Court declared that directors' incorrect evaluation of business risk did not violate directors' duty of oversight.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, A Comparative Perspective on the Limitations of the Duty of Oversight – A Comment on Lisa Fairfax (2013)
scope_conditions: comparison of German and Delaware case law on business risk

subjectOf.text: Delaware's signalling of expected conduct could be dramatically improved by adopting a moderate rather than near insurmountable standard for liability in cases involving breaches of the duty of oversight.
subjectOf.abstract: signaling of expected conduct29 could be dramatically improved with a moderate standard for liability in cases involving breaches of the duty of oversight.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, A Comparative Perspective on the Limitations of the Duty of Oversight – A Comment on Lisa Fairfax (2013)
scope_conditions: breaches of the duty of oversight

subjectOf.text: If the liability standard were lowered, directors and officers would take their increased personal liability exposure into account and could be incentivized to engage in less risky behavior.
subjectOf.abstract: Directors and officers would take their increased personal liability exposure into account and could be incentivized to engage in less risky behavior.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, A Comparative Perspective on the Limitations of the Duty of Oversight – A Comment on Lisa Fairfax (2013)
scope_conditions: a moderate liability standard for oversight breaches is adopted

subjectOf.text: Increasing oversight liability would give courts an opportunity to clarify the oversight doctrine, so that it could evolve into a mature and coherent doctrine rather than remaining immature and incoherent.
subjectOf.abstract: With an increase in liability, courts would also have an opportunity to clarify the oversight doctrine.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, A Comparative Perspective on the Limitations of the Duty of Oversight – A Comment on Lisa Fairfax (2013)
scope_conditions: more oversight suits reach the merits

subjectOf.text: Increased liability is no panacea and cannot alone adequately address the central shortcomings of the duty of oversight and of corporate governance in the United States, because heightened liability does not give part-time outside directors the capacity to monitor complex corporations.
subjectOf.abstract: Increased liability is no panacea and cannot, alone adequately address the central shortcomings of the duty of oversight and corporate governance in the United States that Professor Fairfax identifies.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, A Comparative Perspective on the Limitations of the Duty of Oversight – A Comment on Lisa Fairfax (2013)
scope_conditions: directors serving part time as outsiders

subjectOf.text: Cost increases and path dependencies may make it nearly impossible to relax the close to insurmountable standard for liability in oversight cases.
subjectOf.abstract: Moreover, cost increases and path dependencies may make it nearly impossible to relax the close to insurmountable standard for liability in oversight cases.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, A Comparative Perspective on the Limitations of the Duty of Oversight – A Comment on Lisa Fairfax (2013)

subjectOf.text: The author endorses the conclusion that attempts to enhance oversight in the United States may fail and that emphasizing improved oversight as a means of enhancing corporate governance could be ill-advised.
subjectOf.abstract: This weighs in favour of Professor Fairfax's conclusion that attempts to enhance oversight in the United States may fail and an emphasis on emphasizing improving oversight as a means of enhancing corporate governance could be ill-advised.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, A Comparative Perspective on the Limitations of the Duty of Oversight – A Comment on Lisa Fairfax (2013)

subjectOf.text: Using court decisions and stable rules to make the oversight role more robust could be insufficient, whereas contractual and quasi law forms of dynamic governance could help improve the duty of oversight.
subjectOf.abstract: Using court decisions and stable rules to make "the oversight role more robust to ensure that directors pay greater attention to their monitoring responsibilities" 49 could be insufficient. By contrast, contractual and quasi law forms of dynamic governance could help improve the duty of oversight.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, A Comparative Perspective on the Limitations of the Duty of Oversight – A Comment on Lisa Fairfax (2013)
scope_conditions: directors are outsiders working part time
